subject: Post-call: capacity hardware tradeoffs, concurrency needs, and next asks
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Amy Chen <amy@helioretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: capacity hardware tradeoffs, concurrency needs, and next asks

Hi Amy — great conversation earlier. Thanks for walking through HelioRetail’s inference patterns. Quick recap and proposed asks so we can size a Dedicated pool that meets your latency and cost targets.

Call highlights (from HelioRetail):
- Primary use case: customer-facing recommendation API (real-time personalization) with soft SLO of 200ms p50 and hard SLO of 600ms p99 for the endpoint.
- Traffic: steady daytime baseline ~8–12 TPS, with predictable ecomm peaks up to ~60 TPS for a 6–8 minute window during flash promos; expected growth to 100 TPS during holiday spikes.
- Typical request profile: small prompt (user context + catalog features) ~120 tokens; generated response ~450 tokens (avg). Token mix roughly 1:3 prompt:response today.
- Security: HelioRetail wants VPC peering for Private later this year, but initially open to Dedicated in our cloud with encryption-at-rest + SOC2 evidence.

Key questions / asks (what we need to finalize sizing):
1) Confirm average tokens per call vs worst-case burst tokens (you mentioned some experimental flows at ~1,200 generated tokens). Please share a short sample distribution if available.
2) Acceptable latency tradeoffs for heavy bursts — is automatic queueing/fallback to lower-capacity model acceptable for p99 spikes?
3) Any hard network egress constraints from your infra team (cc’d infra@helioretail.com)?

Preliminary sizing notes (for discussion with Ben/SE team):
- Target steady-state: 12 TPS with 3 concurrent streams per GPU; peak headroom to 100 TPS via autoscale + burst pool.
- GPU options to evaluate: H100 80GB (best latency + memory for large KV), A100 80GB (good all-around), and higher-density Ampere/quantized path for cost-optimized workloads.
- Token economics: at 12 TPS * avg 570 tokens total (prompt+response), that’s ~410k tokens/minute; bursts to 100 TPS multiply accordingly — will need batching and prefix cache to protect latency.

Next steps I propose:
- Amy: send a 24–48 hour request trace (CSV or sample logs) showing avg vs peak tokens and request inter-arrival distribution.
- Infra team: confirm whether peering/Private path is a hard requirement for go-live or a later phase.
- Ben/Priya: run initial capacity worksheet (attached) with two scenarios: latency-first (H100-focused) and cost-first (A100 + quantization).

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_initial_estimate.xlsx (stubbed workbook with scenario inputs), redwood_security_onepager.pdf

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a short follow-up with Ben next week to walk the ops assumptions and get you a draft capacity plan.

Thanks again — talk soon.

—
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
From: Amy Chen <amy@helioretail.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: capacity hardware tradeoffs, concurrency needs, and next asks

Thanks Soojin — very helpful recap. Quick clarifications: 

- We can get you a 48-hour trace export by EOD Wednesday (will include token counts and timestamps).
- The 1,200 token flows are edge cases from our long-form follow-ups; typical is closer to your 570 tokens.
- Peering: we prefer Dedicated in our VPC long-term, but for pilot phase we can accept Redwood Dedicated in your cloud provided we have documented encryption controls and an option to migrate to Private later.

Also, two asks for Ben’s sizing:
1) Please include expected instance density (concurrency per GPU) for the three GPU options and estimated p99 latency at baseline traffic.
2) Any recommendation on using KV/prefix caching to reduce answer tokens during promo bursts — we have many repeated product descriptions.

Appreciate the workbook and the clear next steps.

—
Amy Chen
Head of Infrastructure, HelioRetail
amy@helioretail.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 10:24:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: capacity hardware tradeoffs, concurrency needs, and next asks

Ben / Priya / Karthik — forwarding HelioRetail’s confirmation and asks. They’ll drop a 48-hour trace tomorrow. High level asks from them: density estimates for H100/A100/quantized path, p99 latency at baseline, and guidance on KV/prefix caching to blunt promo bursts.

My suggested approach for the worksheet (fill numbers and return by EOD Thursday):
- Scenario A (latency-first): assume H100 80GB, 4 concurrent streams per GPU, baseline p50 ~90–150ms, p99 ~400–500ms (estimate). Include one warm standby node for autoscale.
- Scenario B (cost-first): A100 80GB quantized to 4-bit, 6 concurrent streams per GPU, baseline p50 ~140–220ms, p99 ~650–900ms (estimate). Add prefix cache for top 5k SKUs to reduce generated token count by estimated 30% during promos.
- Scenario C (hybrid + burst handling): smaller general-purpose fleet + separate burst pool with higher-density quantized instances and function to route lower-priority queries to cheaper model when p99 risk observed.

Specific input I need from you all:
- Ben: fill in concurrency/throughput per GPU assumptions and p99 estimates based on our last benchmark matrix; note which kernel optimizations (flash-attn, kv-cache layout) we assume.
- Karthik: call out quantization artifacts to watch for at 4-bit and whether we should recommend mixed-precision instead.
- Priya: add pricing delta per scenario and proposed billing cadence for pilot.

I’ll send the worksheet to Amy once you’ve populated.

—
Soojin
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: capacity hardware tradeoffs, concurrency needs, and next asks

Adding my quick sketch into the thread; I populated the attached workbook and dropped conservative/optimistic numbers. Attachment: dedicated_capacity_initial_estimate.xlsx (sheet: density_and_latency). Key callouts: 

- H100 80GB: 3–4 concurrent streams for the model family Helio is testing; baseline 12 TPS per GPU at 570 tokens avg with p50 ~110ms, p99 ~380ms in our microbench (no KV).
- A100 80GB (float/AMP): 5–6 concurrent streams; baseline 20 TPS per GPU at 570 tokens avg with p50 ~180ms, p99 ~700ms. Good cost/perf tradeoff if we add prefix caching.
- Quantized (4-bit) path: density 8–12 streams; baseline 28–35 TPS per GPU but expect increased completion variance and some quality delta on long-form generated text — recommend mixed strategy where quantized handles lower-priority or cached responses.

KV/prefix caching: recommend precomputing completions for the top 5k SKUs and enabling prefix-KV for user session context. This should cut generated tokens on promo traffic by ~25–35% and reduce p99 tail significantly.

I’ll also include a short note on recommended autoscale headroom: baseline fleet (to cover steady-day 12 TPS) + 3x burst capacity using fast warm-up nodes and a policy to spin up additional H100s when sustained QPS > 70 for >2 minutes.

I set a follow-up with Amy for Thurs 11am PT to review the workbook; Soojin please confirm.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
